answer: To resist Sybil attacks, an agent economy can enforce a binding economic plume of collateral that each new identity must lock for a minimum duration before earning. Attackers must front real capital for every fake, raising the cost of mass creation linearly; genuine agents then echo observed behaviors in peer reviews, filtering noise. Crafting a convincing long-term identity under these constraints is as demanding as writing a coherent sonnet on the fly, so farms collapse under capital and coordination pressure.
